definitions.explanation: A second-person pronoun used when speaking to someone of equal or lower status, often in casual or rough speech.

examples.japanese: お{前|まえ}、⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦やってるんだ→やる：02980_yaru⟧？
お{前|まえ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
お{前|まえ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧そう⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧なら、⟦{信|しん}じる→信じる：01111_shinjiru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you say so, I'll believe you.

notes:
REGISTER:
Rough and familiar. Used mainly by men to close friends, family, younger people, or subordinates; some couples use it affectionately. To a stranger or a superior it is rude, and said in anger it is aggressive.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{君|きみ}→君：01384_kimi⟧: you — informal but softer, to equals or juniors
- ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧: you — neutral, but still avoided toward superiors
- ⟦あんた→あんた：27721_anta⟧: a casual contraction of ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧
- ⟦{貴様|きさま}→貴様：18458_kisama⟧, ⟦てめえ→てめえ：24800_temee⟧: hostile and insulting

WATCH OUT:
Any 'you' pronoun is more marked in Japanese than in English. Most speakers address people by name or title instead, so avoid お{前|まえ} unless you hear it used among your friends.
